department: Department of Computer Science, School of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences

deadline.value: School of Graduate Studies sets April 1 as the Fall application deadline for international F-1 degree-seeking applicants (unless an earlier program deadline applies); Morgan's Application Deadlines portal lists May 1, 2027 for Advanced & Equitable Computing, PhD (Fall 2027), and SGS funding applications are due April 30.
deadline.quote: Application deadlines for the School of Graduate Studies (SGS) are as follows (unless earlier deadline dates are indicated by the individual programs): ... International, degree-seeking (All F-1 in and out of USA) Fall - April 1

also.quote: Advanced & Equitable Computing, PhD Saturday, May 1, 2027 Fall 2027 Graduate Advanced & Equitable Computing, PhD

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Computer Science or Data Science; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: The Department of Computer Science advises prospective students to contact faculty directly regarding an adviser and financial support (and form a four-member advisory committee by the end of the first year).
supervisor.quote: For adviser and financial support, please contact the faculty directly.

funding.value: Graduate assistantships (TA/RA, $21,000 doctoral stipend plus tuition award up to 9 credits/semester excluding university fees) and fellowships require a separate School of Graduate Studies funding application (due April 30 for Fall) and are not guaranteed.
funding.quote: SUBMISSION OF A FUNDING APPLICATION DOES NOT MEAN YOU WILL BE APPROVED. The decisions will be based on program selection and availability of funding per each program. | Graduate assistantships for doctoral and master's degree students pay a stipend ($21,000-doctoral $12,000-master's) Tuition awards do not pay for university and miscellaneous fees.

entry_route.value: Requires 60 graduate credit hours beyond a bachelor's degree or 36 credit hours beyond a master's degree.
entry_route.quote: Candidates for the Ph.D. in Advanced Computing degree must complete a minimum of sixty (60) academic credit hours beyond the bachelor’s degree or thirty-six (36) credit hours beyond the master’s degree

notes: Offered in both on-campus and remote/online modalities; covers AI/ML, data science, cybersecurity, quantum computing, and HPC. Spring admission deadline is December 1.
name: Advanced and Equitable Computing
